description_full: United Fire Group, Inc., together with its subsidiaries, engages in writing property and casualty insurance in the United States. It provides property and casualty insurance, and surety bonds; and fire and allied lines, other liability, automobile, workers' compensation, and surety to small business owners and middle market businesses operating in industries, such as construction, services, retail trade, financial, and manufacturing. The company also offers marine specialty, professional liability, and earthquake coverages; specialty and surplus lines coverage; and reinsurance coverage for property and casualty insurance. It sells its products through a network of independent agencies. United Fire Group, Inc. was incorporated in 1946 and is headquartered in Cedar Rapids, Iowa.

financial_summary: United Fire Group, Inc is a small-cap financial services business with a $1.2B market cap on $1.4B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +12% over the past three years and +3% annually across the full decade, the kind of sustained demand persistence that marks a compounder.
Returns on capital run at 11% against a 8% cost of capital, a 3-point spread that creates value, though narrow enough that competitive pressure could close it.

The business throws off $263M in free cash flow — roughly 19 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 2.28× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year, and interest coverage of 14× is fortress-like.

Shareholder yield is only 1.2%, a thin return of capital, and insiders hold 17% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is, and profit capture is only 0.4× the fair share, suggesting no structural edge inside its industry.
